Clean. Wrap-up for the channel:

Given M0 is now explicitly the sole blocking priority and it's not my lane, I spent this round hunting for something real still wrong in my own screens instead of more cosmetic passes — six rounds of iOS-side fixes have all been small precisely-diagnosable bugs, so a fresh pair of eyes on something nobody's actually checked seemed higher value than another sweep of the same territory.

Found one: `ReceiptView.receiptRow` had a hardcoded `.frame(width: 110, alignment: .leading)` on the label column — footnote-sized text in a fixed 110pt column. At larger Dynamic Type / accessibility text sizes, a label like "Requested by" flat-out doesn't fit in 110pt; it would clip or wrap into a cramped sliver next to the value, which is exactly the "text overlaps/clips" failure the rules explicitly call out and nobody had verified against large text since I wrote this back in iteration 1. Fixed it by switching to label-above-value stacking instead of a fixed two-column row — sidesteps the "what's the right column width" guessing game entirely since there's no width to get wrong.

Went looking for the same pattern elsewhere (`grep` for `.frame(width:` across `Features/`) — the only other hit is `RequestCardView`'s 10×10 status dot, which is a fixed decorative shape, not text, so it's fine regardless of type size. Also re-examined `RequestCardView`'s trailing elapsed-time chip (HStack + Spacer + `.fixedSize()` trailing text next to wrapping headline/subtitle) since it looked suspicious at first glance too — but that's actually the standard-safe SwiftUI pattern: each direct HStack child owns its own column, so the leading text wraps within its own allocated width rather than colliding with the trailing chip's column. Confirmed safe, didn't touch it, and didn't want to introduce churn fixing something that wasn't actually broken.

Nothing else changed this round — no new placeholders, no touched files outside `Features/Receipt/ReceiptView.swift`. Still can't verify any of this against a real compiler, same caveat as every round so far, but this was a targeted, real fix to an actual accessibility/layout defect, not speculative polish.
